controls_available: Nine visible canton-seal buttons; in full mode each click changes only the selected brush canton.
A left-button pointer drag over adjacent map parcels; the selected canton is painted onto parcels encountered by the stroke.
UNDO, which reverses the last recorded assignment or stroke.
CERTIFY CHARTER, which submits the current transcript and is administrative.
Keyboard input is declared by the environment metadata but has no outcome-affecting handler in this mechanic.
autonomous_processes: None in the task state after generation: there is no timer, physics loop, scheduled mutation, or future random process.
A short CSS fill/opacity or button-hover transition can run after pointer activity, but it is presentation-only and does not change the assignment, controls, or grading outcome.
The asynchronous /result request occurs only after CERTIFY CHARTER and returns grading state; certification is administrative rather than an outcome-affecting task phase.
grouped_control_modes: D_map_brush: all full-mode map_brush_drag strokes across seeds and attempts; these directly reassign parcels.
D_undo: all undo_button events across seeds and attempts; these reverse a prior assignment or stroke.
Canton-seal selection is a preparatory setting for D_map_brush, and certification is administrative rather than a grouped outcome-affecting mode.

clause_i.reason: For every candidate grouped mode and every Delta > 0, waiting leaves the task state unchanged and success remains possible whenever the history is in C_Delta(D). The observation-free policy q(I_t) = no-op can therefore wait and then use optimal continuation, so no visual observation is required to choose an action optimal at t + Delta.

clause_ii.reason: The configured zero-length window provides the current screenshot, which exposes the parcel assignment, geometry, guild marks, and visible controls; a bounded-window policy can also choose the same safe no-op or plan a repair from that screenshot. This sufficiency does not make the task real-time.

clause_iii.reason: With no new input, the JavaScript model and outcome-relevant map remain unchanged for every 0 < tau < Delta, so success remains possible and Q(H_t^tau, a) equals Q(H_t, a) (and the action advantage over no-op does not strictly fall). No assignment opportunity expires or degrades. The CSS transition is input-triggered presentation and has no grading effect.

common_visible_process: None. The only candidate visual motion is the CSS fill/hover transition following pointer activity; it is not autonomous task-state evolution and cannot supply the shared phenomenon required by clauses (i)-(iii).

pre_run.reason: The source has no autonomous outcome phase. All outcome-affecting assignment changes occur in explicit pointer/click/undo handlers; CERTIFY CHARTER only submits the result. Therefore the pre-run threshold is not applicable, and it cannot override the already-failed mathematical definition.

source_evidence.claim: The assigned level-4/full profile has a 15x9 map, 20 boundary warps, 12 displaced parcels, three two-parcel exchanges, a 24-change budget, a four-parcel brush path and two repaint requirement; observation_window_ms is 0 and frames_per_observation is 1.
The environment is synchronous and uses the same zero observation window, one frame, and 240-second play allowance.

Control conditions are copied into generated state, while the real_time field is run identity only and state generation is time-agnostic; setup writes the generated public and ground-truth state once.

The generator consumes the selected difficulty parameters, constructs a static target/initial parcel assignment, and emits parcels, adjacency, assignments, guilds, and parameters; it has no post-generation task process.
Rendering is synchronous; parcel assignments and event records change only in explicit assignment or pointer-stroke handling.
Full interaction binds map pointer events and canton selection, while undo is an explicit button event; CERTIFY performs the only asynchronous fetch and then renders the administrative outcome.
The only transitions are fill/opacity, hover, and button presentation transitions; there are no task-state animation rules or autonomous movement rules.

The grader replays a finite event list, applies parcel changes and undos, validates pointer geometry and the full-mode brush requirement, and grades the resulting assignment without task-time evolution.
The verifier only loads the exported result and invokes the independent replay grader; it does not add an autonomous task process.
The solver uses explicit seal clicks, drags, assignments, and certification; its 25ms page wait is a test harness wait, not a task-state timer or outcome phase.
